50/S0.subgoal: Explain the purpose of the lecture and the four-stage process for building a realistic walking-behavior model for system-controlled VR navigation.

50/S1.subgoal: Describe the empirical study used to collect real walking data, including participants, corridor setup, painting stops, and video recording.

50/S2.subgoal: Explain how the video data were analyzed and why the resulting walking pattern is called the slow-in-slow-out pattern.

50/S3.subgoal: Explain how the slow-in-slow-out pattern is modeled with a Fourier series and how visual gain converts actual walking speed into perceived visual speed.

50/S4.subgoal: Describe the validation study comparing constant and instantaneous speed, and explain that the model improves realism and preference but does not alone solve cybersickness.

50/S5.subgoal: Summarize the main points of this part of the lecture and preview the next part on cybersickness minimization.
